newsitem.title: FINLAND: DEUTSCHE MORGAN SAYS SEES NO MARKKA APPRECIATION.
newsitem.headline: DEUTSCHE MORGAN SAYS SEES NO MARKKA APPRECIATION.

text.p: German bank Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said in a global foreign exchange research note on Monday it did not expect the Finnish markka to appreciate.

Many operators have recently said strong fundamentals such as a massive trade surplus and rapid growth could push the markka higher, but Deutsche said its valuation models called NATREX (Natural Exchange Rates) on quarterly data showed a 3.00 central equilibrium DEM/FIM rate at end-1996.
At 1145/0845 GMT on Monday, the markka traded at 2.9750 per mark.

"Following from this, and the requirement that a country maintain its exchange rate within normal fluctuation bands for two years prior to EMU, we do not believe that the FIM will be revalued," the bank said.

It said the misalignment was not severe "and does not suggest that the FIM is chronically undervalued, nor that a realignment is necessary before Finland considers fixing its intra-European exchange rates at the outset of EMU".
Arbitrage should prevent the spot rate from deviating to any significant or prolongued extent from the 3.04 per mark central parity rate, assuming steady key interest rates, it said.
"Of course, if the central bank does hike rates, then this will allow the FIM to appreciate, but ... we do not expect FIM rates to diverge to any meaningful extent from DEM rates," it added.
